title: New York
blurb: Lower Manhattan sits between the Hudson and the East River. The East River is a tidal strait, and the harbour floods and ebbs through the Narrows four times a day.

title: San Francisco
blurb: The Financial District stands on filled land at the foot of Telegraph, Russian and Nob Hills. Every flood and ebb of the bay passes the city on its way through the Golden Gate.

title: Seattle
blurb: Downtown Seattle climbs a steep bluff above Elliott Bay. The bay opens to Puget Sound, a deep fjord where the tide moves water through narrow passages.

title: Vancouver
blurb: Downtown Vancouver fills a peninsula between Burrard Inlet and False Creek. The tide runs fast through First Narrows under the Lions Gate Bridge.

title: Boston
blurb: Much of central Boston is built on filled land. The harbour is a shallow, island-filled bay with a tidal range of about three metres.

title: Miami
blurb: Brickell and downtown Miami line Biscayne Bay, a shallow lagoon behind the barrier island of Miami Beach. Offshore, the Florida Current carries the Gulf Stream north.

title: Chicago
blurb: The Loop sits on flat lake plain at the mouth of the Chicago River. Lake Michigan has almost no tide, and its currents come from the wind.

title: Dublin
blurb: The Liffey runs east through the city centre and the Docklands into Dublin Bay, between the long harbour walls of the Great South Wall and the Bull Wall.

title: London
blurb: The City of London and Southwark face each other across the Thames. The river here is tidal: at spring tides the water rises and falls by about seven metres, twice a day.

title: Lisbon
blurb: Lisbon climbs seven hills above the Tagus estuary. The river narrows to about two kilometres here before it opens to the Atlantic.

title: Amsterdam
blurb: The canal ring of Amsterdam lies at about sea level, behind dikes and locks. The IJ, the old harbour, separates the centre from Amsterdam-Noord.

title: Venice
blurb: Venice stands on more than a hundred small islands in a shallow lagoon. The Adriatic tide enters the lagoon through three inlets in the barrier islands.

title: Istanbul
blurb: Istanbul spans the southern end of the Bosphorus, where the Golden Horn joins it. Surface water flows south from the Black Sea toward the Sea of Marmara.

title: Dubai Marina
blurb: Dubai Marina is a dredged canal lined with towers, next to the artificial islands of Palm Jumeirah on the shallow, warm Persian Gulf.

title: Mumbai
blurb: South Mumbai fills the tip of a peninsula that was once seven islands. Back Bay and Marine Drive face the Arabian Sea, where the spring tide range is close to five metres.

title: Singapore
blurb: Marina Bay was made by land reclamation at the mouth of the Singapore River. Offshore, strong tidal currents run east and west through the Singapore Strait.

title: Hong Kong
blurb: The towers of Central and Wan Chai stand on a narrow strip of reclaimed land under Victoria Peak. Victoria Harbour separates Hong Kong Island from Kowloon.

title: Tokyo
blurb: Shiodome and Shibaura face Tokyo Bay, where the Rainbow Bridge crosses to the reclaimed island of Odaiba. The bay is a nearly closed basin with a weak tide.

title: Sydney
blurb: The city centre runs north to Circular Quay on Sydney Harbour, a drowned river valley. The Harbour Bridge crosses to the North Shore.

title: Rio de Janeiro
blurb: Botafogo and Urca sit between granite domes: Sugarloaf Mountain at the mouth of Guanabara Bay, and Corcovado to the west. Copacabana faces the open Atlantic.

title: Cape Town
blurb: The City Bowl lies between Table Bay and the sheer north face of Table Mountain, about a kilometre high. The cold Benguela Current flows north along this coast.
